content:
maria: quick thread — I'm prototyping a 'view lifecycle' change that binds saved views to route+model combos instead of just storing raw queries. goal: make per-route/per-model dashboards auto-update with routing/quota previews and avoid stale pins. thoughts?

sam: sounds promising. curious how binding will affect saved queries that are used across multiple routes — do we duplicate views or have a single view with multiple bindings?

jordan: i'd prefer a single view object + bindings array. server applies bindings at read-time. avoids dupes and lets us attach per-binding telemetry hints (sample_rate, provenance).

tyler: big +1 for per-binding telemetry. current problem: when you apply a saved view the telemetry context loses the original query provenance and sampling, so quota previews are misleading. we need to carry a small "telemetry_hint" bag.

maria: agreed. proposed payload (rough):

```json
POST /v2/console/views
{
  "name":"Errors by model",
  "spec": {"filters":[{"field":"status","op":"=","value":"error"}]},
  "bindings":[{"route_id":"route-123","model_id":"llama-70b","sample_rate":0.05}],
  "telemetry_hint":{"provenance":"saved-view:1719251111","default_sample":0.05}
}
```

This keeps telemetry provenance server-side and lets routing policy layer surface correct quota/preview numbers.

sam: nice. one ergonomic question: how do we show this in the UI? when a user opens a saved view, do we show which binding was applied? what if multiple bindings match?

jordan: UI suggestion: top bar chip like "Applied to route-123 · llama-70b" with a chevron to pick alternate bindings. default picks the most specific match (route+model), fallback picks route-only or global.

kevin: migration concern: existing savedqueries have no binding. we should fallback to global behavior and surface a small migration CTA: "Bind this view to a route for preview accuracy". allow batch migration API.

maria: rollout plan idea: feature flag a new API header X-View-Binding:enabled which opt-ins servers to the binding semantics; do canary for internal orgs first, then gradual. also add an A/B metric to ensure quota estimates match reality.

tyler: about sampling, we should not override runtime sampling—only annotate payloads so downstream telemetry service can reconcile. i.e. do not force sample = 0.05 client-side, just provide hint.

maria: good catch. we'll keep it advisory. also need to decide on authz: who can create bindings? product owners only? ops?

jordan: probably creators + team admins; bindings touch routing, so restrict to route owners. UI should show a disabled binding button with a tooltip if you lack perms.

sam: quick edge case: what about ephemeral compare sessions where user tweaks filters? we should avoid creating persistent bindings unless user explicitly saves as bound view.

maria: yep — ephemeral preview uses binding resolution but does not persist unless user clicks 'save as bound view'.

kevin: implementation note for API folks: we might expose an endpoint to list candidate bindings for a view: GET /v2/console/views/:id/candidates -> returns [{route_id, model_id, priority}] so UI can show alternatives.

maria: perfect. can someone sketch the DB shape and minimal API changes? jordan/tyler? i'd like a quick PR this week.

jordan: i'll sketch a migration: add table view_bindings(view_id, route_id nullable, model_id nullable, sample_rate nullable, created_by, created_at). server-side resolution picks best match with scoring: +100 for exact route+model, +50 for route-only, +10 for model-only, +0 global.

tyler: i'll add telemetry_hint plumbing and a small contract to events: {view_id, binding_id?, provenance, hinted_sample}.

maria: sweet. i'll file a design doc and wire up a tiny prototype in console. tagging this for a brief sync tomorrow 10am. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled canary flag flip for X-View-Binding at 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z (internal orgs only).
